ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence on every director, officer, 25% or greater beneficial owner, operator, and source-of-funds provider; identity verification must be performed in accordance with FINTRAC compliance standards; screening must be conducted against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canadian Autonomous Sanctions Lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, OFAC SDN List, and applicable domestic sanctions registries; determination must be made whether any person is a domestic or foreign politically exposed person or head of an international organization; unusual and suspicious transaction reporting obligations apply; records must be retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (ACR) / Alberta Corporate Access online name search portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, the name must end with the mandatory legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC' for an unlimited liability corporation; names may be in English, French, or bilingual; non-Latin scripts are not accepted for registry filing, but a Latin-script transliteration may be submitted if it is clearly identifiable, not confusingly similar to existing names, and otherwise compliant with Alberta corporate name regulations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS corporate name search report is valid for 90 days; there is no statutory extension mechanism, so a new search report and re-filing are required after expiry. If a name is rejected because it is confusing, prohibited, or not distinguishable, the applicant should file an administrative review request with the Director of the Alberta Corporate Registry through the Corporate Access portal, attaching a fresh NUANS report, an alternative proposed name, and any consent letters from registered entities or regulators. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant must select a new name or may pursue judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited permissibility. Alberta requires a physical registered office address within Alberta, not a post-office box, where service of process may be effected and statutory records are accessible. A virtual-office provider can supply a physical street address and document maintenance, but an equity crowdfunding portal is subject to Alberta Securities Commission and FINTRAC regulatory expectations requiring a substantive principal place of business with staff and infrastructure; mail-forwarding-only virtual offices will not satisfy the licensing and AML/CFT substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 80% within the first 18 months of operation, because an equity crowdfunding portal is a regulated securities and money-services-adjacent platform subject to unannounced on-site inspections by the Alberta Securities Commission, applicable self-regulatory organizations, and FINTRAC enforcement visits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9; applicable sections 5 (incorporation), 6 (articles), 15 (registered office), 101 (directors), 117 (officers); Unlimited Liability Corporation provisions under Part 2.1 of the ABCA
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1), Notice of Registered Office (Form 2), and Notice of Directors (Form 3)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the ABCA; an unlimited liability corporation must issue at least one share, but no paid-up capital amount is mandated. Escrow of investor funds is not part of corporate formation; such escrow is imposed as a securities licensing condition under Alberta crowdfunding rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED that the incorporator and sole subscriber hereby subscribes for 1,000 Class A Common Shares at CDN $0.01 per share, representing the initial paid-up capital, and the Board accepts the subscription and directs issuance of share certificates. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office be established at the address stated in Form 2 Notice of Registered Office and that such address be the statutory records address. FURTHER RESOLVED that the directors appoint a Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting, with authority to open bank and escrow accounts and execute regulatory filings. CERTIFIED as a true extract of the First Board Resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Corporate Name Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Name Search Request through the Corporate Registry System; obtain an Alberta Name Search Report and reserve the proposed corporate name for 90 days. Verify that the name includes 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' and is distinct from existing active corporate names.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or confused with an existing name, file a new Name Search Report for an alternative name and resubmit within the same application package; ACR offers a reassessment review within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Articles of Incorporation and Statutory Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / Qualified Legal Counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form 1 Articles of Incorporation with the unlimited liability clause, authorized share structure, classes of shares, restrictions on business, and number of directors. Prepare Form 2 Notice of Registered Office and Form 3 Notice of Directors, ensuring all initial directors have executed consents.
required_dossiers: Signed consent of each initial director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any drafting defects by filing amended articles before submission; if forms are rejected, revise according to ACR deficiency comments and resubmit without additional fees within the correction window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Incorporation Filing and Pay Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed Forms 1, 2, and 3 to the Corporate Registry System; remit the prescribed incorporation fee by credit card or secured electronic transfer; confirm the electronic receipt and capture the assigned corporate file number.
required_dossiers: Executed Form 2 Notice of Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ACR issues a deficiency notice, correct the specified items within 30 days; if the 30-day period lapses, the filing may be deemed abandoned and a new submission with a new fee must be made.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate of Incorporation and Verify Corporate Existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation from the Corporate Registry System; verify the legal name, date of incorporation, jurisdiction, and corporate file number. Place the certificate in the corporate minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not generated within SLA, contact the ACR contact center to escalate; a duplicate certificate may be requested through Form 54 (Request for Certified Copy) with a nominal fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish Registered Office and Maintain Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / Registered Office Address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the physical registered office at the address specified in Form 2 and accept service of process; set up the corporate minute book containing the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles, Notices, and register of directors. Ensure the registered office is open during business hours.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File a new Notice of Registered Office within 30 days of any change; if service of process at the registered office fails, the ABCA requires filing a corrective notice or the corporation may be administratively dissolved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt First Board Resolution and Approve Share Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the first written board resolution accepting the share subscription, setting the initial share issuance, approving the registered office, and appointing officers. Record the resolution in the minute book and have it signed by all directors.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director fails to sign, obtain a written consent of the remaining directors or hold a short-notice meeting; the resolution may be ratified retrospectively by unanimous board consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue Share Certificates and Maintain Securities Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Issue share certificates for the subscribed 1,000 Class A Common Shares, record the name, address, number of shares, and transfer restrictions in the central securities register. Affix the corporate seal where required by the articles.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If there are discrepancies in share records, cancel the affected certificates and reissue new ones only after board approval; for disputes, an application may be made to the Alberta Court of King's Bench under the ABCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Federal Business Number and Provincial Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online / Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with the CRA Business Registration Online portal to obtain a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number and GST/HST account. If the corporation has employees, register for the payroll deductions account; complete provincial corporate tax registration where applicable.
required_dossiers: Board Resolution authorizing tax account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the registration, correct the business identification information and resubmit using the same business number; CRA reassesses the request within 15 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Occupancy Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Licensing Department of Calgary, Edmonton, or other Alberta municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence classifying the activity as an internet financial intermediary. Submit the lease agreement or virtual office contract and obtain building occupancy clearance and fire safety certificate for the physical work location.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or virtual office contract
Fire Safety Certification for the leased premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality denies the licence because of zoning classification, obtain a zoning confirmation letter from the landlord or apply for a minor variance; appeal the denial to the municipal licensing appeal board within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Equity Crowdfunding Portal Registration to the Securities Regulator
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the ASC firm registration application using Form 33-109F6 and the equity crowdfunding portal schedule under Alberta crowdfunding rules, along with the platform control framework, AML/KYC program, and escrow arrangement. Respond to ASC comment letters and obtain a decision document authorizing portal operations before offering securities.
required_dossiers: Escrow agreement with a Canadian chartered bank
Form 33-109F6 Firm Registration and portal schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ASC issues a comment letter or deficiency notice, provide amended disclosure and internal controls within 10 business days; coordinate a pre-filing meeting with ASC staff and resubmit the revised registration package.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Securities Commission, Registration Division; and the Municipal Licensing Department of the applicable Alberta city
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Alberta Equity Crowdfunding Portal Registration (ASC Rule 45-501 and National Instrument 45-110) together with Municipal Business Licence for Financial/Internet Intermediary

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category 3 Office and Financial Intermediary: no manufacturing, no effluent discharge, no emissions point sources, and no specific EIA registration required for a digital crowdfunding portal operating from a licensed office location.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC discharge from normal operations; comply with municipal air quality bylaws; electronic waste must be disposed through a licensed Alberta recycler; if on-site servers are used, maintain HVAC thermal standards under ASHRAE guidance and ensure no ozone-depleting substance releases.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code and local municipal fire department life-safety inspection; structural load inspection stamped by an Alberta professional engineer for any server room or electrical concentration area; workplace clearance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code including first aid, emergency evacuation, and ergonomic compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; official portals: Business Registration Online (BRO), Represent a Client, GST/HST NETFILE, and My Business Account at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency. Alberta-specific authorities: Alberta Corporate Registries (Alberta Corporate Account Registry - ACAR) for incorporation and Alberta Treasury Board and Finance for the 8% Alberta corporate income tax (2% small business rate on the first CAD 500,000) and for the absence of any Alberta provincial sales tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A ULC obtains the statutory 9-digit Business Number (BN) and GST/HST program account through (i) one-stop electronic application via Business Registration Online (BRO), (ii) paper Form RC1 - Request for a Business Number - filed with the Sudbury Tax Centre, or (iii) an authorized representative acting through Represent a Client. Mandatory GST/HST registration arises when the portal's Canadian-sourced taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (Excise Tax Act ss. 240(1), 241, 242); voluntary registration is available to a non-resident that carries on a business in Canada, makes a taxable supply in Canada, or holds an interest in Canadian intangibles, and permits full input tax credit recovery. The BN is the single federal/provincial TIN; Alberta issues no separate provincial tax identifier. Concurrently, the ULC must maintain its Alberta corporate record and file any required T2 corporate return or, after a partnership election, T5013 partnership information return.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. A ULC is by default an incorporated taxpayer under Part I of the Income Tax Act (entity-level taxation at federal and Alberta provincial rates), but may elect under ABCA s. 39 to be deemed not to be a corporation, with each shareholder deemed a partner and the portal's fee income flowing through on a current basis. Territorial scope: resident shareholders are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident shareholders are taxed only on Canadian-source income attributable to the Alberta permanent establishment (ITA ss. 2(3), 115). Tax-exempt zone: none; no Canadian special economic zone status applies to Alberta fintech or crowdfunding operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (1) ABCA s. 39 partnership election - requires unanimous shareholder consent and that all shareholders be resident in Canada at the time of the election, filed with CRA; converts the ULC into a deemed partnership for income tax purposes, with reporting migrating from T2 to T5013. (2) ETA s. 273 election - filed with CRA to deem the ULC and its shareholders a single GST/HST partnership registrant, mirroring the income-tax pass-through. (3) US check-the-box - a US shareholder may file IRC Form 8832 or Form 8858 to treat the Canadian ULC as a partnership or disregarded entity for US federal tax purposes, producing a hybrid entity profile that must be reconciled with Canada's hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.4(3), 94B and OECD BEPS Action 2). (4) Default no-election - the ULC remains a corporation in Canada while flowing through to a sole US member, enabling consolidated US federal filing and Canadian corporate allocation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST - Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; Alberta applies only the 5% federal GST with no provincial component (no PST/RST in Alberta).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - worldwide and Canadian-sourced taxable supply threshold for small supplier status, measured per calendar quarter and trailing four quarters; excludes exempt financial services supplies for threshold purposes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada imposes no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction controls. CRA relies on post-audit verification of electronic records under ETA s. 286 and voluntary adoption of the PEPPOL e-invoicing framework in the B2G segment. GST/HST returns are filed electronically through GST/HST NETFILE; remittances above CAD 25,000 must be made by EFT or wire. A crowdfunding portal must retain machine-readable digital ledgers covering issuer contracts, escrow statements, investor KYC files, and fee schedules for CRA inspection within 30 days of demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The portal's service fees to a non-resident, non-registered person are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 9 provided the service is not rendered to an individual present in Canada, does not relate to real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada, and is not supplied to a non-resident GST/HST registrant. Fees charged to Canadian-resident issuers are generally subject to 5% GST; fees that constitute the arranging of an equity issuance may be exempt as a financial service under Schedule V, Part VII, s. 1, so substance and documentation determine taxability. Refund mechanics: zero-rated outputs permit full input tax credit recovery on the GST/HST return, and any excess net ITC refund is paid under ETA s. 170 within 30 days of filing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - CES electronic filing (paper form G13/B13A) with the Canada Border Services Agency where tangible goods are exported; for services, replaced by FINTRAC EFT report for cross-border payment flows
Commercial invoice / Canada Customs Invoice (Form B5-2) accompanied by the signed portal service agreement and fee schedule with the non-resident issuer
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (goods-only route); for services, substitute with time-stamped platform logs, KYC files, and the foreign issuer's certificate of residence
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by a Canadian chartered bank or authorized foreign-exchange dealer evidencing USD/CAD settlement through the banking channel
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess zero-rated claims within 4 years (ETA s. 298), extended to 7 years for misrepresentation and without limitation for fraud; if contemporaneous export evidence is absent, the 0% rate is clawed back to 5% of the full fee, GST is assessed as collectible, daily compound interest accrues under ETA s. 280 (prescribed rate plus 4%), and gross-negligence penalties apply under ETA s. 285 (greater of CAD 250 and 25% of net tax sought), with additional false-statement penalties under ETA s. 327.1. Criminal prosecution for wilful evasion under ETA s. 327 may impose fines of 50%-200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years on indictment; equity crowdfunding portals also face Alberta Securities Commission exempt-market-dealer audits, FINTRAC money-services-business examinations, and securities licence sanctions that can cascade into reassessment and licence revocation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) - central monetary authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) - federal prudential regulator of banks; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) - AML/KYC and cross-border transaction reporting authority; Alberta Treasury Board and Finance - provincial financial services oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible under a free-floating exchange rate regime; there is no foreign-exchange control law, no central bank conversion permit, and no capital-flow approval mechanism. Current-account transactions (trade in goods/services, dividends, interest, royalties, management fees) and capital-account transactions (equity subscriptions, intercompany loans, portfolio investment) may be executed freely in any currency. Profit remittance by an Alberta ULC is unrestricted, subject only to the corporate solvency tests under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, to withholding tax on payments to non-residents under Income Tax Act Part XIII, and to applicable treaty relief under the Canada-US Tax Convention. All cross-border electronic funds transfers at or above CAD 10,000 are reportable to FINTRAC by the financial intermediary; non-resident investments of controlling scale may trigger Investment Canada Act notification or review.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio on export receipts or other foreign-currency earnings. A ULC may retain export and crowdfunding revenues indefinitely in CAD, USD, EUR, or any other currency in domestic or offshore accounts, and may convert at commercial rates through any authorized bank or registered foreign exchange dealer. The only binding obligations are FINTRAC reporting of cross-border electronic funds transfers and currency movements of CAD 10,000 or more, and the maintenance of complete wire-transfer records for any transfer exceeding CAD 1,000, plus compliance with federal sanctions and OSFI anti-money-laundering guidance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility with significant legal constraints. Canada does not recognize the EU/UK EMI passport, and offshore digital EMIs cannot hold client funds, clear CAD, or access domestic payment rails without either (i) entering into a regulated sponsorship arrangement with a Schedule I Canadian bank or (ii) obtaining FINTRAC registration as a money services business and, where applicable, Bank of Canada authorization under the Retail Payment Activities Act. For escrow-grade crowdfunding funds, securities laws in Alberta compel custody with a Canadian financial institution or a registered securities firm; an offshore EMI is therefore legally disqualified from serving as primary treasury custodian and may only provide auxiliary disbursement or FX conversion support.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the de facto standard for a high-risk, special-license equity crowdfunding portal: the ULC's authorized director, corporate secretary, and every 25%-or-greater ultimate beneficial owner must complete an in-branch identity interview in Alberta, or a remote-video session approved by the bank's National Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) unit, combined with reliable independent identity verification permitted under FINTRAC rules. Foreign-resident directors are generally required to appear in person at a Canadian branch, or to deliver an apostilled and notarized identity dossier supplementing a video interview. Pure remote onboarding is available only where all signatories are Canadian residents with an existing banking relationship and the portal holds a final Alberta Securities Commission registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or UBO with politically exposed person (PEP) status
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced Due Diligence pack: apostilled passport, police clearance from country of residence, bank reference from a G7-regulated financial institution, source-of-wealth statement, PEP declaration, and confirmation that all funding wires will originate from the UBO's regulated bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Alberta Securities Commission license or exemption not yet evidenced
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified legal opinion from Canadian securities counsel confirming registration as an exempt market dealer or funding portal, or a valid National Instrument 45-110 / 45-107 prospectus-exemption filing; escrow agreement executed with a qualified custodian; and an undertaking to segregate investor funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crowdfunding float exposing the bank to money-mule, layering, or sanctions risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC money services business registration, automated investor AML/sanctions screening procedures, per-investor subscription limits aligned with crowdfunding caps, segregated trust-account undertaking with no commingling, and a quarterly independent compliance audit report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial equity capital injection into the ULC
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital verification file comprising the share subscription agreement, board resolution approving the issuance, three-month source-of-funds bank statements from the remitting regulated institution, sworn beneficial-ownership declaration, and the ULC's certificate of allotment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident institutional investors inject equity capital into the ULC via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 wires bearing the explicit purpose reference 'EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION - CA AB ULC' together with the share subscription agreement and allotment certificate; no Bank of Canada approval or exchange-control permit is required. Canadian banks treat such receipts as capital-account inflows and may request the underlying transaction documents for KYC/EDD completion. For retail equity-crowdfunding investors, inbound funds must be routed exclusively into the segregated capital escrow account through Payments Canada Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) ACH credits or direct bank wires, never into the ULC operating account, in accordance with Alberta securities custody requirements. FINTRAC cross-border electronic funds transfer reporting triggers at CAD 10,000; all incoming payments must include the remitter's legal name, account number, and regulated-bank originator information.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements are executed through (i) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border supplier and invoice payments; (ii) commercial letters of credit and standby LCs governed by UCP 600 where trade finance is extended to startups and portfolio companies; (iii) Lynx (the Canadian real-time gross settlement system replacing LVTS) for high-value CAD domestic disbursements; and (iv) USD clearing via the Canadian bank's US correspondent network over CHIPS or Fedwire for US-dollar payables. Because the CAD is freely deliverable, the treasury may settle invoices in CAD, USD, or EUR provided the commercial documentation is consistent and the bank's trade-transaction AML exceptions are satisfied.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forwards on CAD/USD and CAD/EUR executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Schedule I Canadian bank
FX swaps (spot-vs-forward and swap-point rollovers) for short-term cross-currency liquidity transformation
Cross-currency swaps to hedge USD- or EUR-denominated equity proceeds into CAD operating and escrow funding
Vanilla FX options (put/call) and zero-cost collars on CAD pairs for budget-rate protection of projected crowdfunding fee revenue

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted to secondary exposures in non-convertible currencies (e.g., CNY, INR) where the underlying receivable is itself non-deliverable; CAD pairs never require NDFs due to full convertibility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the corporation's incorporation date (calendar window recalculated annually).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a registry penalty and the ULC is placed in inactive status; failure to file for two consecutive annual cycles allows the Registrar to administratively dissolve the company after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Portal Report with Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the ULC's fiscal year-end (December 31 for calendar-year filers).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers securities enforcement action, administrative penalty, and possible suspension or revocation of the crowdfunding portal registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed; maintained in statutory books and available for inspection by Alberta Corporate Registry or ASC upon request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed and signed by the board no later than the annual return filing due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain and audit statutory registers is an offence under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; inspectors may compel production, and directors may be held personally liable for defaults.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the ABCA, a non-offering ULC may waive auditor appointment through an annual unanimous shareholders' resolution, but the ASC crowdfunding portal licence mandatory audit condition overrides this waiver, making an independent audit by a registered public accounting firm compulsory every fiscal year regardless of revenue or asset size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the Canadian Accounting Standards Board (AcSB) for the portal's financial statements; ASPE may be used only if the ASC exemption is obtained. The ULC must maintain a complete double-entry accounting system in accordance with Canadian GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Within 15 days of any share transfer or creation of an Individual with Significant Control (ISC), the ISC register must be updated. On each anniversary, the ULC shall conduct a reconciliation of the ISC register, the share ledger, and the director registers; results are recorded in a directors' resolution and retained. Share transfers in the ULC must be approved by directors, registered in the share ledger, and disclosed in the next annual return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 260 – USD 580 per annum depending on agent and complexity.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 – USD 25,000 per annum for a licenced crowdfunding portal with escrow settlements.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined general rate (15% federal Part I general rate after abatement and general rate reduction plus 8% Alberta general corporate income tax rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 11% combined federal/Alberta rate if the Alberta ULC qualifies as a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) and claims the small business deduction on the first C$500,000 of active business income. No statutory tax holidays are available to an equity crowdfunding portal in Alberta. Non-resident ownership exceeding 50% disqualifies CCPC status and restores the 23% general rate. Canadian non-capital losses may be carried forward 20 years and back 3 years.
